passages.text: “Not by being slack, or with little strength may this be realized—extinguishment, the release from all suffering.
passages.note: Freedom from suffering takes real effort

passages.text: “Geese, herons, and peacocks, elephants and spotted deer—though their bodies are not equal, they all fear the lion. So it is for humans—if a little person is wise, they’re the truly great one, not the fool with a good body.”
passages.note: Worth lies in wisdom, not appearance or size

passages.text: “Why are you angry? Don’t be angry! It’s better to not be angry, Tissa. For this spiritual life is lived in order to remove anger, conceit, and denigration.”
passages.note: Letting go of anger and wounded pride

passages.text: “And how, Senior, is living alone fulfilled in detail? It’s when what’s in the past is given up, what’s in the future is relinquished, and desire and greed for present incarnations is eliminated. That’s how living alone is fulfilled in detail.”
passages.note: True solitude is letting go of past and future

passages.text: “Sir, I’m an old man, elderly and senior. I’m advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life. My body is ailing and I’m constantly unwell. I hardly ever get to see the esteemed mendicants. May the Buddha please advise me and instruct me. It will be for my lasting welfare and happiness.” “That’s so true, householder! That’s so true, householder! For this body is ailing, swaddled in its shell. If anyone dragging around this body claimed to be healthy even for an hour, what is that but foolishness? So you should train like this: ‘Though my body is ailing, my mind will be healthy.’ That’s how you should train.”
passages.note: Ageing and illness: keeping the mind healthy
